title: Database startup Supabase raises $150M, acquires Turso
key_facts: Supabase, which sells a paid, managed version of the open-source PostgreSQL database, raised $150 million.
Singapore's GIC sovereign wealth fund led the round, joined by Alphabet's CapitalG, IronArc and SquarePeg.
Supabase also agreed to buy fellow database startup Turso for an undisclosed sum.
Turso offers a database for AI agents built on SQLite, a small open-source database that runs on low-power devices and starts almost instantly.
Supabase also introduced Supabase Compute, a new cloud service that gives long-running AI agents hosted sandboxes; SiliconANGLE says Turso could help it.
Supabase will use the money for employee liquidity and new AI agent features.
Co-founder and CEO Paul Copplestone wrote in a blog post that agents are spinning up millions of databases.
quote_evidence: Supabase announced the raise today alongside another business milestone: it has agreed to buy fellow database startup Turso for an undisclosed sum.
“Agents are spinning up millions of databases to power the prototypes, explorations, dashboards, and apps they’re building,”
Supabase will use the proceeds from its funding round to provide liquidity for employees and build new AI agent features.
why_it_matters_hint: Shows money flowing to database tools built for AI agents, and a consolidation of two database startups.
notes: Single outlet (SiliconANGLE) relaying the company announcement. Deal is "agreed", closing not stated. Price undisclosed. The "Turso could help Supabase Compute" point is SiliconANGLE's own analysis.
